accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop through a native <label for> on the first thumb; with a range each thumb also gets an aria-label ("<label> minimum", "<label> maximum").
announcements: error text is announced once when it appears (persistent aria-live=polite region); value changes are announced by the native slider
aria: each thumb is a native range input: role slider with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuenow from the native control
aria-orientation="vertical" on each thumb when vertical
aria-describedby -> description and error ids (same root)
aria-invalid="true" when an error is set
a thumb cannot cross the other: the lower one is clamped to the upper one
accessibility.focusRingVisible: On keyboard focus of a thumb; 3px ring in slider.focus-ring.color.

formAssociation.note: ElementInternals: setFormValue with the value, or one entry per thumb for a range; the inner input anchors validity (errorMessage sets customError); formResetCallback restores the default values; disabled is not submitted.

keyboard.Enter: submits the form (implicit submission; the control has no form owner in its shadow root, SB-0009)
keyboard.Home / End: jump to the minimum or maximum

accessibility.missingNameWarning: Dev-only console warning, once, when label is empty.
accessibility.targetSize: The thumb is 16px inside a 24px press area (WCAG 2.5.8); the track is also pressable and keys work without any pointer.

antiPatterns.alternative: Show the value in the label or beside the slider
antiPatterns.why: The thumb position alone is not exact

antiPatterns.pattern: A slider with only a few discrete choices

useCases.when: Pick a number where approximate position matters more than the exact digit
Pick a lower and upper bound
People may need the exact number

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.notes: Vertical stack with the field gap.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: Native <label for> pointing at the first thumb.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: Positions the track, range and thumbs; also takes pointer presses on the track of a two-thumb range.

anatomy.name: range
anatomy.notes: Filled part: from the start to the thumb, or between the two thumbs.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: Native <input type="range">, one per value, drawn as a round handle. Receives focus and keys.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Persistent polite live region; text appears when invalid.

change.note: Value committed (key press, release). Re-dispatched from the host because native change is not composed (NativeControl).

input.note: While a thumb moves. Native and composed; a press on the track of a range emits an equivalent event from the host.

openQuestions.answer: Yes: APG slider and multi-thumb slider patterns, realized with native range inputs.
openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG)?

openQuestions.answer: Two native range inputs overlaid on one track, each a real slider with its own name; the lower one is clamped to the upper one. A press on the track moves the nearest thumb.
openQuestions.question: How is a range built?

openQuestions.answer: "<label> minimum" and "<label> maximum" through aria-label; the visible label points at the first thumb. A later change can add props to localize them.
openQuestions.question: How are thumb names built for a range?

openQuestions.answer: A comma-separated list of numbers in the value attribute, one thumb per number; the property returns an array of numbers.
openQuestions.question: What is the value format?

openQuestions.answer: A vertical slider is three times the semantic unit size.slider.vertical-length (64px), 192px, because the scale has no 176px step. Logged as drift.
openQuestions.question: Vertical length against the foundation scale?

errorMessage.note: Error message. Setting it marks the field invalid.

hideLabel.note: Visually hides the label; it stays the accessible name.

label.note: Visible label and accessible name. With two values each thumb is named "<label> minimum" and "<label> maximum".

name.note: Form field name. A range submits one entry per thumb under this name.

orientation.note: Direction of the track. Vertical grows upward.

required.note: Accepted for form-associated parity; a slider always has a value, so it never blocks submission and shows no asterisk.

value.note: Current values as numbers separated by commas: "40" for one thumb, "20,80" for a range. One thumb per number. Empty means the minimum. Not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset.

focus-visible.note: 3px solid ring around the focused thumb.

contract.summary: A slider for picking a number, or a range with two thumbs, built on native range inputs, with label, description and error built in, taking part in forms.

# Plan: Slider (planning gate)

Status: Approved under SB-0011 (owner pre-approval, 2026-11-08).

## Scope
`sb-slider`: native `<input type="range">` per value inside one shadow root, drawn with a custom track and filled range; horizontal and vertical; one or two thumbs; form-associated.

## Files (in build order)
| Step | File |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | `src/components/slider/Slider.stories.ts` |
| 2 | `playwright/tests/slider/slider.behavior.spec.ts` (first, must fail) |
| 3 | `src/components/slider/Slider.scss` -> `Slider.styles.ts` |
| 4 | `src/components/slider/Slider.ts`, `index.ts` |

## Test plan
Name and label click, one slider role per value with distinct names for a range, keyboard (arrows, Home, End, Page keys), vertical (ArrowUp increases, aria-orientation), min/max/step, thumb clamping, track press on a range, filled range geometry, input/change composed, focus ring, form value (one entry per thumb), reset, disabled, disabled fieldset, error validity, axe.

## Accessibility deviations
- Unfilled track below 3:1 (visual choice); thumb and range meet it.
- Solid focus ring.

## Open questions (recommendation first)
- Range as two native inputs, names via aria-label (contract Q1, Q2).
- Semantic tokens added: `size.slider.vertical-length` (64px unit; the control is 3 units) and `size.slider.track` (6px).
